description: Enforce clean worktree invariant for task completion, add agent cleanup loop, rewrite merge action with full squash-landing + fast-forward push delivery pipeline, and commit spec-sync changes.

tasks.title: Enforce clean worktree invariant and agent cleanup loop
tasks.description: Add a post-action git status --porcelain check in WorkExecutor.executeOne(). After any action returns successfully, verify the worktree is clean before marking the task completed. For agent-backed tasks (mohist/acp-agent) that leave a dirty worktree, enter a bounded cleanup loop: send a constrained follow-up prompt to the same agent session instructing it to inspect uncommitted changes, commit task-related ones, or revert unrelated ones, without starting new work or pushing. Re-check cleanliness after each attempt up to maxCleanupAttempts (default 3). Deterministic actions that leave dirty worktree fail immediately with structured evidence. Produce structured dirty-worktree evidence on failure: a JSON object with staged, unstaged, and untracked file arrays (from git diff --cached --name-only, git diff --name-only, git ls-files --others --exclude-standard) and the cleanupAttempts count.
acceptanceCriteria: Non-agent deterministic tasks that leave dirty worktree fail immediately with structured dirty-worktree evidence listing staged, unstaged, and untracked files
Agent-backed tasks (mohist/acp-agent) that leave dirty worktree enter the cleanup loop instead of failing immediately
Cleanup follow-up prompt explicitly constrains the agent: no new work, no push, commit task changes or revert unrelated ones, report commit SHA or no-change
Cleanup loop reuses the same agent session (no new session created); loop is bounded by maxCleanupAttempts
Cleanup succeeds when git status --porcelain becomes empty; task completes with cleanup attempt count in result
Cleanup exhaustion produces structured failure evidence with the cleanupAttempts count and categorized file lists

Unit tests in packages/runner/tests/executor-cleanup.spec.ts cover: clean task completion, dirty deterministic failure with evidence, cleanup success on first attempt, cleanup success after multiple attempts, cleanup exhaustion, and same-session reuse verification
tasks.notes: The clean check goes after action success and before artifact capture in executeOne(). Agent-backed detection uses work.uses check against 'mohist/acp-agent'. The cleanup prompt builder is a helper in executor.ts, not a separate action. Use the existing git() helper from packages/runner/src/actions/git.ts for git commands.

tasks.title: Rewrite merge action with full fetch-rebase-land-push delivery pipeline
tasks.description: Rewrite mergeAction in registry.ts to implement the complete delivery pipeline. The new flow: (1) Source clean guard — run git status --porcelain, fail with phase=source-cleanup and dirty-worktree evidence if not clean. (2) Fetch — git fetch <remote> <target>. (3) Rebase — git rebase <remotes>/<target> on source branch; on conflict invoke the existing mergeConflictResolverRunner agent to resolve, with bounded retries; exhaust unresolved conflicts fail with phase=rebase-conflict. (4) Land — checkout the fetched remote target commit as detached HEAD, git merge --squash the rebased source branch, git commit with the merge message. (5) Validate landing — verify clean worktree, no in-progress merge/rebase, and landing commit parent equals fetched remote target commit; failure fails with phase=landing-validation. (6) Push — when push:true, push the exact landing commit via git push <remote> <landingSha>:refs/heads/<target> (fast-forward only, no --force). (7) Verify remote ref — git ls-remote to confirm. (8) Remote-advanced retry — if push is rejected, fetch the new remote target, rebase source again, regenerate landing commit, and retry push within maxPushRetry (default 5); exhaustion fails with phase=push. Every failure produces phase-classified structured evidence. Update the default workflow YAML to add push:true and remote:origin to the integrate:merge with block. Remove the old commitPendingSourceChanges call — merge no longer auto-commits dirty changes.
acceptanceCriteria: Source worktree dirty at merge entry fails immediately with phase=source-cleanup and lists dirty files; no fetch, checkout, rebase, or push operations execute
Fetch failure produces phase=fetch structured evidence
Clean rebase onto fetched remote target succeeds and proceeds to landing; rebase conflicts invoke the configured agent resolver with conflict file list
Resolved rebase conflicts after agent resolution succeed; unresolved conflicts after maxConflictRetries produce phase=rebase-conflict with unresolved file list
Squash landing commit is created on detached HEAD from the fetched remote target commit, has exactly one parent matching the remote target SHA, and uses the configured merge message
Landing validation fails with phase=landing-validation if worktree dirty, merge/rebase in progress, or parent mismatch
With push:true, fast-forward push uses exact git push <remote> <sha>:refs/heads/<target> syntax without --force or --force-with-lease; remote ref is verified after push
Push skipped when push:true is not configured; delivery facts include landing SHA but no remote ref verification
Remote-advanced rejection triggers full retry (fetch → rebase → land → push); exhaustion after maxPushRetry produces phase=push with retry count and last known remote SHA
Phase failure evidence includes phase field (source-cleanup, fetch, rebase-conflict, landing-validation, push) and phase-specific structured data
Default workflow YAML (mohist-default.workflow.yaml) has push:true and remote:origin on integrate:merge with block

Existing merge tests in packages/runner/tests/merge.spec.ts updated for new pipeline; new tests cover each failure phase, rebase conflict resolution, successful push, remote-advanced retry, and push-disabled path
tasks.notes: Reuse the existing mergeConflictResolverRunner (ACP agent) for rebase conflict resolution. The landing step creates a detached HEAD — after commit, no branch is updated locally. Push uses the landing commit SHA directly. The old commitPendingSourceChanges helper is removed entirely — merge no longer silently commits dirty leftovers.

tasks.title: Commit spec-sync changes after deterministic copy
tasks.description: Update openspecSyncAction to run git add specs/ and git commit -m "Sync OpenSpec specs from change delta" after copyDirectory completes. If the specs directory has no changes to commit (already synced), return success with a no-change marker. The executor's post-action clean worktree check from T-001 will verify the commit succeeded and the worktree is clean.
acceptanceCriteria: After copyDirectory copies spec files to the worktree specs/ directory, the action runs git add specs/ followed by git commit
When specs directory has no changed files after copy (already up to date), the action returns success with a no-change indication
Unit tests in packages/runner/tests/openspec.spec.ts cover: commit after sync with changed files, no-change when already synced, and git command failure handling
tasks.notes: Use the existing git() helper for git commands. The commit scope is limited to specs/ (git add specs/) to avoid capturing unintended files from prior dirty tasks.

tasks.title: End-to-end regression test reproducing issue #102 shape
tasks.description: Write an integration test in packages/runner/tests/ that reproduces the full issue #102 failure chain and verifies the new system prevents it: (1) An agent-backed task returns success but leaves uncommitted changes in the worktree. (2) The executor detects the dirty worktree and enters the cleanup loop. (3) The cleanup prompt is sent to the same agent session; the agent commits the changes. (4) The executor verifies clean worktree and marks the task completed. (5) A subsequent merge action validates the source worktree is clean and proceeds through the full delivery pipeline (fetch, rebase, squash land, fast-forward push). (6) The merge task completes with push evidence. Also test the failure paths: cleanup exhaustion blocks merge, and dirty worktree at merge start fails with phase=source-cleanup.
acceptanceCriteria: Integration test: agent task leaves changes → cleanup loop sends follow-up prompt → agent commits → executor verifies clean → task completes
Integration test: agent task leaves changes → cleanup loop exhausts → task fails with structured dirty-worktree evidence → merge does not proceed
Integration test: merge action receives dirty worktree → fails with phase=source-cleanup → no git operations beyond the clean check execute
Integration test: clean agent task → clean merge source guard → full pipeline (fetch, rebase, squash land, push) completes with push delivery facts in task output
All integration tests pass on clean git repository setup
tasks.notes: Use the existing setMergeGitRunnerForTest and setMergeConflictResolverForTest patterns for mock git and agent. The mock git runner should simulate the full real git command sequence for each test path. Tests should use a temporary real git repository or mock all git calls through the test runner injection points.
